Hi Alicia — thanks for sending this through and for the clear appendix. A few technical clarifications that will help us produce an informed counterproposal:

1) "Uptime" definition: Can you confirm whether your measurement point is end-to-end (client to application) or only Redwood-served endpoints? In our proposed model we prefer provider-side measurement (per-region node health) with mutually-agreed monitoring hooks.

2) Credits calculation: Your table's top-tier credit assumes a single incident triggers a maximum monthly credit. We typically cap cumulative credits to avoid cascading exposure from repeated short incidents. Would you consider a per-incident cap plus an overall monthly cap?

3) Response windows: We can commit to a 1-hour ack for P1, but remediation/restore timelines vary by incident class. Would Ventra accept an "acknowledge" vs "remediate" distinction (ack within 1 hour, restore target within 6 hours for most infra-related P1s)?

4) Maintenance windows: Our standard model allows rolling maintenance across regions with notice windows; emergency hot-fixes can be applied with shorter notice but we usually exclude them from credits if required for security patches. Please confirm if Ventra considers security/emergency patching as creditable downtime.

If you can reply to the points above, I'll loop in our SRE runbook snippets and recommended credit caps.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Evelyn / team — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clarifying questions, Jonas. Below are Ventra's responses and a few small concessions we can make to expedite execution.

Responses: 
- Measurement point: Ventra will agree to a hybrid measurement approach — provider-side primary with end-to-end sample checks for disputed incidents.
- Credits: we'll accept a per-incident cap of 10% of monthly fees and a hard monthly cap of 25% (matches our internal procurement comfort).
- Response windows: we're comfortable with an "acknowledge vs restore" distinction. Ventra prefers ack in 1 hour; restore targets can be negotiated per incident class — your proposed 6-hour restore for infra P1s is acceptable as a starting point.
- Maintenance: Ventra will exclude security/emergency patching from creditable downtime provided Redwood supplies the root cause and timeline in the incident report within 48 hours.

Concessions: Ventra will relax the "two blackout windows per quarter" restriction to allow three planned blackout windows per quarter up to 10 total hours if we provide 14 days' notice.

Next steps:
1) We'll take your counter language on credits/attribution and send a DocuSign envelope with updated Order Form and an accompanying summary page.
2) If Redwood signs, Ventra will start provisioning the monitoring hooks and arrange a technical handoff call with SRE the week of 4/8.
